sources.citation: Larsen, Robert & Marlys Larsen. 1982 [1985]. Orokaiva legends, lessons and grammar notes (Workpapers in Papua New Guinea Languages 30). Ukarumpa: SIL. (Rosetta Project excerpt)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Grammar Notes p.77 sec. 1.3: 'In Orokaiva words, the first syllable is the most stressed.. The second greatest emphasis is on the third syllable in words longer than two syllables.' Lessons p.64: words are 'in the Sose or Central Orokaiva dialect'. Not Aeka.

sources.citation: Larsen, Robert & Marlys Larsen. 1977. Orokaiva phonology and orthography. In R. Loving (ed.), Phonologies of five P.N.G. languages (Workpapers in Papua New Guinea Languages 19), 5-28. Ukarumpa: SIL.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.12 sec. 5.1: 'Stress is non-phonemic. The primary stress is always on the first syllable of each word.' But p.5: 'The dialect studied was that spoken by the people who live between Agenehambo and Wasida on the road from Popondetta to Kokoda' = Orokaiva proper, not Aeka.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-190 (submitted by Rachel Hiley, SIL PNG): split [ork] Orokaiva into [okv], [hkk] Hunjara-Kaina Ke, [aez] Aeka; adopted 2008-01-14.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Identity: 'Aeka is 72% lexically similar to Orokaiva. However, Aeka speakers consider their language as different from Orokaiva. They reported very low comprehension of Orokaiva' (p.2); based on a 7-day SIL survey in the Aeka area.
